channel.title: PVR Labs
channel.description: Java performance experiments, engineering articles, and developer tools from PVR Labs.

item.title: What Prometheus and Grafana Actually Do for Your Web App
item.description: Understand how Prometheus and Grafana collect and visualize application metrics, how they work with Express, FastAPI, Django, and Spring Boot, and when simpler monitoring is enough.

item.title: I Used an AI Agent Skill to Migrate Spring PetClinic Persistence From JPA to SQL
item.description: An AI agent migrated Spring PetClinic persistence to SQL. All 17 packaged H2 checks passed, but independent code review found two repository bugs.

item.title: Spring Boot Actuator Metrics vs. Prometheus: Which Endpoint Should You Use?
item.description: Use Spring Boot Actuator’s JSON endpoint to inspect a meter and its Prometheus endpoint for ongoing collection. Includes setup and troubleshooting for both.

item.title: OpenJ9 vs. HotSpot on a 256 MiB Debian VM
item.description: A short exploratory comparison of Java 25 runtimes, memory and startup on a 256 MiB Debian VM.

item.title: Spring PetClinic, Rewritten Without Spring Boot or Hibernate
item.description: Rewritten with CoilBase + Jex + Jdbi: 59% less application RSS and 85% smaller deployment in this experiment. Results measure the combined application-stack change.

item.title: MariaDB vs PostgreSQL on Small VPSes: What My Low-Memory Experiments Found
item.description: Short database-only experiments compare MariaDB and PostgreSQL memory use and read workloads on 256 MiB and 512 MiB VMs.

item.title: JPA Memory Experiment Revisited: Hibernate Without Spring Data JPA
item.description: Jdbi used about 55–58 MiB less RSS than direct Hibernate in a shared demo app on a 512 MiB Linux VM. Method, results and limitations.

item.title: PostgreSQL 18 on a Small VPS: Two Low-Memory Tuning Strategies
item.description: A short PostgreSQL 18 comparison on a 512 MiB VM: two low-memory configurations, four active connections, and measured memory and query latency.

item.title: Five Java Stacks on a 512 MiB VPS: Same Business Logic, Different Footprints
item.description: Shared services across Javalin, Jex and Micronaut, with Spring JDBC and Micronaut Data references: two HotSpot and native runs per stack on a 512 MiB VM.

item.title: H2's Built-in Connection Pool vs HikariCP: Is There a Memory Cost?
item.description: A short Linux comparison of embedded H2's native pool and HikariCP.

item.title: Importing 1 Million CSV Rows: Scriptella 1.7 vs Pandas, JDBC, and Native Loaders
item.description: Scriptella 1.7.0, JDBC, Pandas + SQLAlchemy, and native loaders compared on one million CSV rows in PostgreSQL and MariaDB. Two local runs, with reproducible results.

item.title: Beyond Optimized Spring Boot: Javalin, Jdbi and a Smaller Java Application
item.description: A database-backed service on a 512 MiB VM: comparing optimized Spring Boot with Javalin and Jdbi on HotSpot 27 and Oracle Native Image 25.

item.title: How Lightweight Can Spring Boot Become? HotSpot 27 and Native Image
item.description: On a 512 MiB VM, the same Spring Boot service used 212 MiB as a JAR, 187 MiB with HotSpot 27 AOT, and 107 MiB as Oracle Native Image on JDK 25.

item.title: How Far Can You Optimize Spring Boot Without Overengineering It?
item.description: Spring Boot on a 512 MiB VM: extracted layout, Spring AOT and a JDK cache cut startup and RSS. MyBatis and H2 follow-ups show where the trade-offs change.

item.title: Telegram health alerts for small VPS apps, without a monitoring stack
item.description: Use StatLite's external API and a scheduled shell script to send Telegram alerts and recovery messages when application health changes.

item.title: Monitoring applications behind Caddy with StatLite
item.description: Monitor HTTP requests, errors and response latency for applications behind Caddy using per-host metrics and StatLite, without changing application code.

item.title: Rewriting batched inserts made PostgreSQL CSV import 1.7× faster
item.description: Enabling reWriteBatchedInserts made a million-row Scriptella import 1.70× faster on PostgreSQL, from 15.995 to 9.409 seconds. Handwritten JDBC was 1.55× faster.

item.title: LeanBar: Same Scripts, Less Memory
item.description: A lightweight Swift and AppKit app that reuses existing SwiftBar scripts, with one local physical-footprint comparison against SwiftBar.

item.title: Java SQL Persistence: Jdbi vs MyBatis vs jOOQ on 512 MiB
item.description: Java SQL persistence comparison: Jdbi, MyBatis and jOOQ in a 512 MiB Javalin application. Two runs each, comparing JVM memory, HTTP latency and code.

item.title: MyBatis vs. jOOQ vs. Jdbi: Java Persistence on 256 MB RAM
item.description: Three Javalin persistence implementations on a 256 MiB Alpine VM: startup, RSS, paging, package size, and application code from one run each.

item.title: Importing a million CSV rows: Scriptella, JDBC, csvsql, and PostgreSQL COPY
item.description: Batched Scriptella loaded a million typed CSV rows in about 15 seconds on PostgreSQL and 10 on MariaDB. JDBC was a few seconds faster, which may be worth a declarative ETL file.

item.title: Javalin vs. Spring Boot on 256 MB RAM: A Practical Java Experiment
item.description: Javalin and Spring Boot with JDBC, H2, and monitoring on a 256 MiB Alpine VM: startup, resident memory, latency, and paging from one run each.

item.title: Reducing PostgreSQL Memory Use by Shrinking Idle Connection Pools
item.description: Two Spring Boot pools released 18 idle connections. PostgreSQL cgroup memory was approximately 29 MiB lower, with a measured cost when traffic returned.

item.title: Can StatLite monitor a Pyronaut Python app?
item.description: A Pyronaut app exposed the Micronaut and Micrometer Prometheus metrics understood by StatLite's existing Micronaut integration.

item.title: Spring Boot, Quarkus, and Micronaut: JDBC on a 1 GiB VM
item.description: Equivalent JDBC apps on Java 25: startup, process RSS, and CPU for Spring Boot, Quarkus, and Micronaut on a 1 GiB Linux VM.

item.title: My API Is Up, but Slow. Is It My Code or the Server?
item.description: Use application and host metrics on one timeline to investigate a slow API on a small server.

item.title: Spring Boot JPA vs JDBC
item.description: On one Mac, a small Spring Boot app used about 90 MiB less RSS with JdbcTemplate than with Spring Data JPA and Hibernate.

item.title: Monitoring a FastAPI App on a Small VPS
item.description: Try practical FastAPI monitoring locally, then run the same small StatLite and SQLite setup alongside an application on a VPS.

item.title: Lightweight Express.js Monitoring Without Prometheus and Grafana
item.description: Chart Express traffic, errors, latency, and Node.js memory with a small /statlite/metrics helper and StatLite, without operating Prometheus and Grafana.

item.title: Spring Boot Extracted Layout vs Jib Exploded Layout
item.description: A short comparison of two filesystem layouts for the same Spring Boot application.

item.title: Spring Boot vs Quarkus at 1 GiB with Swap Disabled
item.description: A short no-swap follow-up to the 768 MiB Spring Boot vs Quarkus memory experiment.

item.title: Spring Boot vs Quarkus on a 768 MiB VM
item.description: A short comparison of Spring Boot and Quarkus memory behavior on a 768 MiB VM with identical JVM limits and a bounded workload.

item.title: Spring Boot Fat JAR vs Extracted Layout vs Gradle Application Distribution
item.description: A quick exploratory comparison of three Spring Boot packaging and launch layouts.

item.title: Spring Boot Fat JAR vs Extracted Layout
item.description: Six paired runs of the same Spring Boot 4.1.1 app on a 256 MiB Alpine VM. The official extracted layout cut median startup 23.3% and first-request latency 34.1%. Settled RSS showed no material difference.

item.title: Spring Boot vs Quarkus on a 512 MB VPS
item.description: Spring Boot and Quarkus ran the same Star Pulse workload on a 512 MB VPS with JDK 25. Quarkus started larger, then had a smaller resident set, while RSS hid swap.

item.title: Your Coding Agent Doesn’t Need 1,476 Lines of Test Output
item.description: A successful test run produced 1,476 lines. The coding agent needed roughly one.

item.title: Your coding-agent quota is at 99%. Now what?
item.description: Continue a local Codex or Claude Code session in ChatGPT or another browser AI chat. AI Badger imports the transcript and current repository context.

item.title: Spring Boot on 256 MB: JDK 25 Compact Headers Tested
item.description: Spring Boot on a 256 MiB VPS with JDK 25 compact object headers, an 80 MiB heap, and swap. Includes a JDK 27 update: compact headers are now enabled by default.

item.title: Spring Boot on a 512 MB VPS: How Lightweight Monitoring Still Fits
item.description: A Spring Boot 3.5 app with JPA, H2, Tomcat, and Actuator ran on 512 MB RAM plus a small swapfile. StatLite stayed around 12 MiB and kept polling.

item.title: Reviewing agent-generated code with an independent second model in VS Code
item.description: Review agent-generated code in VS Code using an independent second model, from complete Git changes to focused, repository-aware follow-up context.
